statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band: December NQ futures sit at the low of an 85.50-point overnight band, a drift of only about 0.27% of the index, with VIX at 15.01 and no volatility expansion.

headline: NQ drifts to the low of a shallow 85-point overnight band after a 52-week high; Tail stays low into the September FOMC minutes
body: The cash Nasdaq-100 closed 6 October at 31,224.69, up 148.24 points or 0.48%, after setting a fresh 52-week high at 31,361.37 and then fading to finish nearer the 31,208.20 session low. Overnight, December NQ futures trade 31,435.75, down 47.50 points or 0.15%, sitting at the 31,435.50 low of an 85.50-point band topped at 31,521.00. That drift is about 0.27% of the index and sits against a falling VIX at 15.01, down 3.29% with a 14.96-15.54 day range, so the structure reads as shallow directional drift rather than repeated extension after failed retracements. Cross-asset evidence conflicts rather than aligns: Asian cash is softer, with the Nikkei 225 at 70,064.14 down 0.88% and the Hang Seng at 24,093.60 down 0.77%, while December ES futures hold 7,876.25, up 0.03%, inside a 9.25-point band. Under the published calibration that conflict raises Stress ahead of Tail. The macro backdrop stays restrictive: the H.15 for 5 October shows the 2-year at 4.89%, the 10-year at 5.26% and the 30-year at 5.59%, while WTI at 90.18 and Brent at 101.40, both up about 0.8%, keep a Middle East supply-risk channel open. The session's catalysts stack in a three-hour window: the 10-year note auction at 17:00 UTC prices into a 5.26% yield, and the September 15-16 FOMC minutes follow at 18:00 UTC, covering a unanimous 25 basis point increase to 3.75-4.00%. Those minutes pre-date softer data since released, including September payroll growth of 29,000 and August core PCE at 3.0%, and futures now price roughly 20-22% odds of an October hike against about 81% odds of at least one more increase by December. A hawkish tone shift is therefore the most credible delayed-second-leg mechanism in this session, which is why the forecast lifts Tail to a conditional 21-23% WATCH band from 17:00 to 20:00 UTC. The shared Finviz context was not used: its latest collection is dated 29 September and is far outside the 90-minute freshness contract, so this assessment rests on independently fetched primary sources, and Confidence is held at 87% rather than higher.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry published Claude assessments. Tail ran 8-16% through the Asian and European hours of 6 October, rose through the U.S. session to a 22% peak at 15:00 UTC with the 15:00 and 16:00 UTC slots mapping to WATCH, then decayed steadily to 10% by 01:00 UTC on 7 October as the index faded off its 52-week high into the close. Stress held a narrow 45-48% band throughout and Confidence stayed between 86% and 88%. Dominant mode ran mixed through the Asian hours, shifted to trend-up from 10:00 to 19:00 UTC on 6 October, and returned to mixed overnight.
outlookSummary: The remaining Asian and European hours are modelled with Tail at 12-14% on contained two-way ranges around the observed 31,435.50 overnight low. Tail lifts to 15-18% across the 13:30 UTC cash open and the first cash hours for opening-range expansion, then to a conditional 21-23% WATCH band from the 17:00 UTC 10-year note auction through the 18:00 UTC September FOMC minutes and the following power hour, which is the published danger window. Risk decays to 17% at the 20:00 UTC cash close and back to an 11-14% overnight baseline, with Stress peaking at 55% alongside the minutes and Confidence declining from 87% to 79% as the horizon extends.
